verdict: Book frozen on stale prints — NPL 32.26%, capital cushion gone.

risk: Court-stayed loan stock understating the printed 32.26% Q1 NPL ratio

runway.unit: bp of CAR buffer above the 10% floor

banker_read.verdict: On the Q1 2026 print NPLs hold 32.26%, system CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio) 1.56% on the Q3 2025 read — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone not thin. Neither refreshes until Q2 disclosure; the new five-year cleanup plan meets a book that borrows less for want of investment scope.

tldr: The book holds frozen — NPL 32.26% on Q1, CAR 844bp under floor.
analysis: The banking book is frozen and the freeze is the story: NPLs 32.26% on the Q1 2026 read, system CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio) 1.56% on Q3 2025 — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither moves until Q2 disclosure lands the court-stayed loan stock that already understates the printed ratio. What is new is the policy answer and the demand signal, and they point opposite ways. The state has floated a five-year plan to clean up the sector — a resolution runway for the SCB (State-Owned Commercial Bank) tail the market has long discounted. Yet banks now borrow less for want of investment scope, and private credit sits at 4.98%: liquidity is not the constraint, creditworthy demand is. A cleanup plan repairs the tail; it does not restart the engine. Dispersion stays the trade — own the private compounders, fade the SCB paper the resolution regime tests first.

title: DSE Markets
verdict: Fresh low on vanishing volume — Tk733cr turnover, no bid.

banker_read.verdict: DSEX slipped 0.07% to 5,769.71, a fresh window low — but the tape has gone quiet, not cracked. Breadth healed to 140 up against 198 down from the 54/318 washout, while turnover caved to Tk733cr, thinnest of the window. Sellers are spent; buyers never came. Stay flat until volume returns on up days.

tldr: DSEX slips to a fresh low of 5,769.71 as turnover caves to Tk733cr.
analysis: The DSE is not crashing — it is emptying out. DSEX printed a fresh window low at 5,769.71, but the day's move was a rounding error at -0.07%, and the internals tell the real story: decliners fell to 198 from the 318 washout, advancers rose to 140 from 54, yet turnover caved to Tk733cr, the thinnest of the window. Abating selling with absent buying is a market that has run out of sellers before it found a buyer. The backdrop explains the vacuum. The easing curve has rallied hard — the 10y down 82bp to 9.42% — and banks now borrow less for want of investment scope while private credit sits at 4.98%. Cheap money is finding risk assets no more than it is finding borrowers: the same demand vacuum, priced in two markets. Stay flat — a low made on Tk733cr is not a bottom to trust until volume confirms it.

chart_read.signal: DSEX slipped 0.07% to a fresh window low of 5,769.71 as turnover caved to Tk733cr; breadth healed to 140 up, 198 down from 54/318.
chart_read.context: A fresh low across the 5,770–5,897 window — the 5,822 floor that broke last week now sits above.
chart_read.implication: Equity desk: a fresh low on record-thin turnover is exhaustion, not a bottom — stay flat until volume returns on up days.

title: T-Bonds & T-Bills

risk: A 10y round-trip back to 10.24% if the single-print rally proves thin
Belly and long supply into FY27 re-steepening the curve

watch: Whether the 10y's 9.42% print holds or mean-reverts toward the 10.24% it sat at all window

5s10s at ~27bp — the flatter slope repricing long-dated fixed-rate books
banker_read.verdict: The long end caught the rally the front led — the 10y collapsed 82bp to 9.42%, flattening 5s10s to ~27bp from ~109bp against a 5y anchored at 9.15%. The 91d bill holds 9.03%, sub-policy across the front. Easing now spans the curve; treat the 10y's single-print jump with care.

tldr: The 10y rallies 82bp to 9.42%; 5s10s flattens to ~27bp, front sub-policy.
analysis: The curve flattened in a single print, and the size of the move demands both attention and caution. The 10y had sat at 10.24–10.25% across the entire window; today it prints 9.42%, an 82bp collapse that drags 5s10s from ~109bp to ~27bp against a 5y anchored at 9.15%. Read straight, the long end has finally caught the rally the front has led for weeks — the 91d bill at 9.03% and the 364d at 9.17%, the whole front sub-policy as BB's easing feeds through. Read sceptically, an 82bp one-day move in an illiquid long bond is as likely a marks artifact as a genuine repricing, and the round-trip risk back to 10.24% is real. Either way the desk conclusion holds: fund term to a front that keeps falling, but do not extend duration into the 10y on a single unconfirmed print. Watch the next auction and a second 10y mark before trusting the flatter curve.

chart_read.signal: The 10y collapsed 82bp to 9.42% from a static 10.24%; the 91d bill holds 9.03% and the 5y 9.15%, flattening 5s10s to ~27bp.
chart_read.context: The 10y sat at 10.24–10.25% across the whole window until today; the front has cut at every recent auction.
chart_read.implication: ALCO: 5s10s flattens to ~27bp on one 10y print — fund term to the front, but confirm the long-end move before extending duration.
